chapter_theme: Seeing the form of Siva (சிவ சொரூப தரிசனம்): the Lord is consciousness, life and all things yet beyond thought, close as scent in a flower; he wakes the seeker, and what is seen is bliss and light beyond turiya, named by every title and none, beyond words.
structure_note: The chapter alternates affirmation and negation: the Lord as nectar, bliss and all things (2856, 2857), his nearness to those who think of him and his waking of the poet (2858, 2859), the bliss-light within turiya (2860), a string of denials (2861), the knowers who reach that bliss (2862), and the state beyond turiya that cannot be told (2863).

2856.reading: Nectar wells up at every hair-root, a bliss that does not waver between difference and non-difference; the greatness of the one whose form the Veda chants lies beyond, past the three primal forms.
2856.nuance: பேதம் அபேதம் (difference and non-difference) are the terms of the debate on how the soul stands to the Lord; the bliss here does not tip to either. ஆதி சொரூபங்கள் மூன்று (the three primal forms) is not fixed by the verse; it may be taken as the three aspects of being, knowing and bliss, or as three forms of the Lord. ஓதும் may go with the nectar ('the nectar spoken of') or simply open the verse.

2857.reading: He is awareness and he is life; he is the union and he is the lovers' sulking; though bound up with all, he cannot be reached by thought, and he stays close as the scent stays in a cluster of flowers.
2857.nuance: புணரும் and புலவி are the love-poetry pair of union and sulking, so the Lord is both moments of love; read so, the line borrows akam language for the soul and God. இணரும் may mean 'joined (with all)' or 'clustered', echoing இணர் (cluster) and துணர் (bunch) in the last line. The scent in the flower is Tirumular's recurrent image for a presence that pervades without being seen.

2858.reading: Keep in mind first the one who stays close; when you think of him he will end your lack; the one of lasting scripture, the Vedic one, the great ascetic, is known through a certainty that stands within the head.
2858.nuance: The opening துன்னிநின்றான் takes up the last word of 2857, linking the verses. மறையவன் மாதவன் can be epithets of Siva (the Vedic one, the great ascetic) or names of Brahma and Vishnu (மாதவன் is a name of Vishnu), which would change the line's sense. சென்னியுள் (within the head) is traditionally taken as the crown centre of yoga; plainly it may mean only 'in the mind'.

2859.reading: With my mind lit as by lightning I woke, and in that waking the peerless Lord, light of himself, Nandi of golden body and coiled matted hair, opened my eyes; how am I to know what came to me?
2859.nuance: நந்தி is both Siva and Tirumular's teacher, so the waking is at once grace and initiation. The last line is compressed: என்னுற்று அறிவன் may be 'how shall I know what befell me' or 'what shall I know of myself', and என்விழித்தான் 'he opened my eyes' or 'he looked upon me'.

2860.reading: Truth, knowledge, the one substance, bliss; the great light of Siva's bliss that does not stay in the mind; pure Brahman, turiya; and within turiya, the great light reached in the turiya beyond it.
2860.nuance: சத்திய ஞான ... ஆனந்தம் matches the Vedantic triad of being, knowledge and bliss, and சுத்தப் பிரம is Vedanta's word; the verse sets them beside சிவானந்தம், as Tirumular elsewhere joins Vedanta and Siddhanta. துரியத்துள் உய்த்த துரியம் (a turiya brought within turiya) is usually taken as துரியாதீதம், the state beyond turiya.

2861.reading: It is not Para, nor the enduring Paraparan, nor strength, nor the bright flame known above, nor the bearer; being all these it is none of them; it is not even Hara, but lies beyond bliss.
2861.nuance: A string of denials in the manner of 'not this, not this': each title of the Lord, even அரன், falls short. உரன் (strength, or knowledge) and தரன் (bearer, or one who holds a rank) are uncertain. தான் அவையாய் அல்லவாகும் keeps the denial from being a simple absence: it is all of them and not them. Even bliss (ஆனந்தம்), which 2860 named, is passed.

2862.reading: One whose knowledge is complete, holding both release and attainment, stands within devotion and within the Supreme; those who stand within the great Shakti, as the tattvas join, pass beyond purification and become knowers of blissful joy.
2862.nuance: முத்தியும் சித்தியும் sets release beside yogic attainment. தத்துவங் கூடலால் (because the tattvas join, or are reached) and சுத்தி யகன்றோர் (those who have left purification behind, or those beyond the purified state) are obscure; the line may mean they no longer need the purifying rites. சுகானந்த போதர் (knowers of joy-bliss) is a compound of Sanskrit terms.

2863.reading: The state beyond turiya is the void where words cease; if one grasps the rare turiya and the beyond, how can one tell of one's own form, which spreads, contracts, does not break open, gleams and turns?
2863.nuance: பாழ் (void, barren waste) is Tirumular's word for the state beyond form. தன் உருவும் may be the form of the self or of the Lord, and the five verbs (spread, contract, not open, shine, turn) may describe its play or simply its being past description; விள்ளா may also mean 'cannot be uttered'.

links.note: Both make the bliss bodily: in 2831 turiya, sweet as milk and honey, soaks every hair-root; in 2856 nectar wells up at each hair-root.
Both end on the Lord who stays as scent in a flower (மலர்க்கந்தம் ... நின்றானே); 304 sets the image after the devotee's babbling praise, 2857 after naming him as all things yet beyond thought.
The Kural names sulking and union as what lovers gain from love; Tirumular, using the same pair (புலவி, புணர்வு), says the Lord is both, carrying love's moments over to the soul and God.
2857 affirms that he is awareness, life, union; 2861 denies him every name, then reconciles the two: being all these, it is none of them.
Both call the state where turiya subsides the void where words cease (சொல்லறும் பாழ்) and say it is hard to know or tell.

source_issues: 2856: line 1 reads மயிரக்கால், a misprint for மயிர்க்கால் (hair-root).
2857 is repeated as 3035 (chapter 223) with two variants that change the sense: புணர்வும் for புணரும் and புலனும் (the senses) for புலவி (sulking).
2862: line 4 reads யகன்றொர், probably for அகன்றோர்.
